summary.text: Sean McCann, a Democratic Michigan state senator from Kalamazoo, won the election for Michigan's 4th District on November 3, 2026, defeating incumbent Rep. Bill Huizenga, and is set to take office on January 3, 2027.
He previously served in the Michigan House and worked in the nonprofit sector, and was term-limited in the state Senate.
He announced his campaign in July 2025 and won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary.

paragraphs.text: Sean McCann was born in Michigan and earned a B.A. in political science from Western Michigan University in 1993.
He worked as executive director of Kalamazoo Friends of Recreation, director of financial development for the American Red Cross, and executive director of the Vine Neighborhood Association.
McCann served on the Kalamazoo City Commission from 1999 to 2008, then in the Michigan House of Representatives (District 60) from 2011 to 2015.

McCann was elected to the Michigan Senate in 2018 (District 20) and took office in 2019; since 2023 he has represented District 19, which includes Kalamazoo and surrounding municipalities. His campaign says the district makes up about one-third of the 4th Congressional District.
In the 2025-2026 session he serves as Majority Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee and chairs the Energy and Environment Committee.
Michigan's term limits barred him from seeking another Senate term. He announced his congressional campaign on July 14, 2025, and defeated Diop Harris II in the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election with 50.1% of the vote to Bill Huizenga's 48.3%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
